fields.meta_description: Build a conditional logic form from a prompt. Fields show or hide by answer, submissions route by rule, and you own the database.
fields.h1: Build a Conditional Logic Form That Asks the Right Questions
fields.hero_description: Describe each rule as you would say it. Emergent builds the conditional logic form, with fields that show or hide on an answer and routing after submit.
fields.features_heading: What a Rule Can Change on the Form
fields.features_subheading: A rule pairs an answer with an action. These six actions cover most of what people ask a form to do.
fields.feature_1:
Fields that appear on the right answer

Show a follow-up field only when an answer calls for it. A yes to food allergies opens a box asking which ones, and a no keeps it hidden and out of the stored response.
fields.feature_2:
Choices that narrow as people answer

Remove options that stop fitting. Once a party is larger than a room holds, that room leaves the dropdown, and a delivery date list drops the days a route is already full.
fields.feature_3:
Conditions with more than one part

Combine answers with AND and OR, such as a budget over $10,000 and a start date inside 30 days. Describe the condition in a sentence and change it later by asking for the edit.
fields.feature_4:
Routing that runs after submit

Send each submission where its answers point. A large deal posts to a sales channel in Slack, while a support issue goes to the help desk inbox with the customer's plan attached.
fields.feature_5:
Required only when it applies

Make a field mandatory when another answer calls for it. A tax ID becomes required once someone picks a business account, and stays optional for anyone signing up as a person.
fields.feature_6:
Rules you can read in your repo

Export the form to GitHub on paid plans with every rule written out as code. A developer can trace why a field showed up for one person and add a condition without starting over.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Forms, Four Kinds of Rule
fields.tab_content_1:
Dose and schedule questions show up after a yes

Owners booking a stay at Pinecrest Pet Lodge answer a question about medication. A no moves them on to feeding. A yes opens three required fields: the drug name, the dose and the times it is given. Staff see the schedule on the dog's record before drop-off, and no booking goes through with the dose left blank.
fields.tab_content_2:
With a guest count over 150, the garden room disappears

Couples planning a wedding at Larkhill Barn type a guest count before they see the room choices. The garden room seats 150. A count above that takes it off the list and leaves the hall and the terrace. Nobody falls for a room the venue cannot offer, and the coordinator stops writing the same apology email.
fields.tab_content_3:
Demos for 200 seats or more go to a rep

Seat count decides what happens when a team asks Northwind for a demo. Requests for 200 seats or more post to the enterprise sales channel in Slack with the company name and seat count. Smaller teams get an email with a link to book a 30-minute walkthrough. Both land in the same leads table.
fields.tab_content_4:
No one over the budget cap reaches question three

Question two on the Riverbend Community Foundation grant application asks for the annual operating budget. Anything above $2,000,000 ends the form with a short message and a link to the foundation's capacity fund. Qualifying applicants move on to the narrative questions, and staff read eligible applications only.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Conditional Logic Form
fields.howto_description: Rules are easier to get right on paper than inside a builder. Sketch them first and the form follows.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write each rule as a sentence
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with the fields every person fills in whatever they choose, such as name and email. Then mark each question that only some people need, and next to it write the answer that should bring it in.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Give every rule a trigger and an action: if the budget is above the cap, end the form and show the referral message. A rule you can read aloud is one a colleague can check. Vague rules turn into bugs later.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Start from the answer, not the field it reveals. When two rules hang off the same question, put them side by side and check they never fight over one field, with one rule showing it and the other hiding it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Hidden answers stay blank in the stored response. Decide what happens when someone fills a field and then changes the answer that revealed it. Clearing the old value keeps reports honest about who was asked what.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your rule sentences into a prompt along with the fields and where each submission should go. Emergent builds the form and its logic together with the table behind them. Ask in plain English when a rule needs changing.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Logic keeps working after someone clicks submit. Pick the answers that change who hears about a response, such as a seat count that sends a lead to sales or an urgent flag that emails the on-call manager.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill the form once for each path, including edge values such as a guest count of exactly 150. Check what was stored after each run, and confirm the right person got each alert. Delete the test rows before sharing the link.

plan.angle: The top 10 is vendor help pages and feature pages (Tally, Slate, ClickUp, Gravity Forms, Jotform), a WordPress plugin listicle and a Notion news post. Each explains where to click inside one tool. None helps someone decide which rules a form needs, what happens to an answer once its field is hidden, or how to test every path before going live. This page treats a rule as a sentence you can read back: a trigger, a condition and an action. Four rule types carry it, each on a real form: a field that appears, a choice that disappears, a submission routed by its answers, and a form that ends early for people who do not qualify. It stays on single-screen field logic and post-submit routing, leaving step-by-step screens to the multi step form page.
